grammar.title: GRAMMAR
grammar.rule_explanation: Bu dialogda Present Perfect va Present Perfect Continuous asosan o'tmishda boshlangan, hozirgacha davom etayotgan simptomlar, yaqinda sodir bo'lgan o'zgarishlar, bemorning oldingi tajribasi va hozirgi klinik vaziyat bilan bog'liq natijalarni ifodalash uchun ishlatilgan. Present Perfect Continuous o'tmishda boshlangan va hozirgacha davom etayotgan yoki yaqinda davom etib kelgan jarayonni, ayniqsa uning davomiyligi yoki takrorlanishini ta'kidlash uchun ishlatiladi.
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: Bu dialogda Present Perfect va Present Perfect Continuous asosan o'tmishda boshlangan, hozirgacha davom etayotgan simptomlar, yaqinda sodir bo'lgan o'zgarishlar, bemorning oldingi tajribasi va hozirgi klinik vaziyat bilan bog'liq natijalarni ifodalash uchun ishlatilgan. Present Perfect Continuous o'tmishda boshlangan va hozirgacha davom etayotgan yoki yaqinda davom etib kelgan jarayonni, ayniqsa uning davomiyligi yoki takrorlanishini ta'kidlash uchun ishlatiladi.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: Present Perfect связывает прошлое с настоящим. Он часто используется для опыта, недавних изменений и результатов, которые важны сейчас. Present Perfect Continuous подчёркивает процесс или длительность действия, начавшегося в прошлом и продолжающегося до настоящего момента.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: have used → qancha yoki qanday natija bo'lgani muhim bo'lishi mumkin 3. She ___ (has been using / has used) her reliever four or five times a day.
grammar.structure_pattern: How long + have / has + Subject + been + V-ing? | Subject + have / has + V3

dialogue.speaker: Doctor
dialogue.text: What has been happening with your breathing?

dialogue.speaker: Patient
dialogue.text: I've been struggling to breathe for about five days, but it has become considerably worse since yesterday evening.

dialogue.speaker: Doctor
dialogue.text: Have you been wheezing as well?

dialogue.speaker: Patient
dialogue.text: Yes. I've been wheezing repeatedly, particularly at night, and I've woken up twice feeling unable to get enough air.

dialogue.speaker: Doctor
dialogue.text: Have you developed a productive cough, fever, or chest pain?

dialogue.speaker: Patient
dialogue.text: I haven't had a fever. The cough has remained mostly dry, but my chest has felt very tight.

dialogue.speaker: Doctor
dialogue.text: How often have you been using your reliever inhaler?

dialogue.speaker: Patient
dialogue.text: I've been using it four or five times a day, whereas I normally use it only occasionally.

dialogue.speaker: Doctor
dialogue.text: Has it been providing lasting relief?

dialogue.speaker: Patient
dialogue.text: It has helped for a short time, but the symptoms have kept returning. Nurse: Her respiratory rate is 26. Oxygen saturation is 91% on room air, and she is speaking in short sentences.

dialogue.speaker: Doctor
dialogue.text: Thank you. Have you ever been admitted to hospital because of asthma?

dialogue.speaker: Patient
dialogue.text: No, but I had an emergency visit about two years ago.

dialogue.speaker: Doctor
dialogue.text: Have you been taking your preventer inhaler regularly?

dialogue.speaker: Patient
dialogue.text: Not consistently. I've missed quite a few doses recently because I've been travelling.

dialogue.speaker: Doctor
dialogue.text: Have you noticed any particular triggers?

dialogue.speaker: Patient
dialogue.text: Cold air has been making it worse, and I've also been exposed to a lot of dust at work.

dialogue.speaker: Doctor
dialogue.text: Have you recently had a cold or another respiratory infection?

dialogue.speaker: Patient
dialogue.text: I had a mild cold last week, but I thought I had recovered.

dialogue.speaker: Doctor
dialogue.text: It sounds as though your asthma control has deteriorated. We need to assess the severity of this exacerbation rather than assuming it is simply another mild attack.

dialogue.speaker: Patient
dialogue.text: Could I be having a serious asthma attack?

dialogue.speaker: Doctor
dialogue.text: Your oxygen saturation and increased work of breathing are concerning, so we need to monitor you closely. Nurse: I'll start continuous oxygen saturation monitoring and prepare the prescribed bronchodilator treatment.

dialogue.speaker: Doctor
dialogue.text: We'll also check your peak expiratory flow if you are able to perform the test safely.

dialogue.speaker: Patient
dialogue.text: Will I need steroids?

dialogue.speaker: Doctor
dialogue.text: You may need systemic corticosteroids depending on your response to the initial treatment and the severity of the exacerbation.

dialogue.speaker: Patient
dialogue.text: How long will I have to stay here?

dialogue.speaker: Doctor
dialogue.text: That depends on how your breathing responds. If your oxygenation improves and your symptoms settle, we may be able to discharge you with a revised asthma plan. Relative: She has been coughing at night for several weeks, even before this attack.

dialogue.speaker: Doctor
dialogue.text: That suggests her underlying asthma may not have been well controlled for some time. We'll review her long-term treatment as well.

dialogue.speaker: Patient
dialogue.text: I understand. I don't want this to happen again.

dialogue.speaker: Doctor
dialogue.text: Exactly. The immediate priority is stabilising your breathing; afterwards, we'll address prevention and inhaler adherence.

tests.question: What is the medical meaning of the term 'struggle to breathe' in clinical consultation?
tests.explanation: 'struggle to breathe' atamasining to'g'ri ma'nosi: nafas olishda qiynalmoq.

tests.question: Which term corresponds to 'balg'amli yo'tal'?
tests.explanation: 'balg'amli yo'tal' ma'nosiga mos keluvchi tibbiy termin 'productive cough' hisoblanadi.

tests.question: Which of the following is the grammatically and clinically standard question to ask about the duration of symptoms?
tests.option_a: How long do you having this symptom?
tests.option_b: How long has this condition been bothering you?
tests.option_c: Since what time you have this problem?
tests.option_d: How many days you are feeling pain?
tests.explanation: Klinik anamnezda davomiylikni so'rash uchun Present Perfect Continuous ('How long has... been bothering you?') to'g'ri shakl hisoblanadi.

tests.question: When evaluating acute pain, what is the best phrasing to assess pain character?
tests.option_a: Is your pain bad or very bad?
tests.option_b: Can you describe the pain—is it sharp, dull, throbbing, or aching?
tests.option_c: Why do you have sharp pain today?
tests.explanation: Og'riq xarakterini aniqlashda shifokor ochiq va taklif qiluvchi variantlar (sharp, dull, throbbing, aching) beradi.
